deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 2 of Grothendieck's preparatory notes for his late-1967 lectures on crystals, which assesses Washnitzer–Monsky (W.M.) cohomology. The previous page credits W.M. with a p-adic cohomology in characteristic 0 for varieties in characteristic p, with coefficients W(k) and possibly a good notion of p-adic torsion. This page lists its formal weaknesses.

(1) The theory is built only from differentials. One lifts a smooth affine X_0 over k to a weakly complete (dagger) algebra over W and takes its de Rham complex. In practice this restricts the theory to smooth X_0.

(2) Because it works only with the de Rham complexes Ω^•, the method seems unable to produce Leray-type spectral sequences for a morphism f : X_0 → Y_0. Such relative tools are what one needs for dévissage arguments in proofs.

(3) Consequently, 'sans doute', W.M. have not yet proved the most basic expected formal properties. The key example is that H^i_WM(X) is finitely generated over W. The next page continues: 'and hence presumably' neither duality nor Künneth. It does concede that they obtain a Lefschetz–Weil trace formula for zeta functions, close to Dwork's method.

The page thus motivates crystalline cohomology. That theory is defined for arbitrary, even singular, X_0 via the crystalline site, is functorial and has relative versions (Gauss–Manin, Leray), so dévissage becomes possible. The following §3 relates W.M.'s heuristics to Grothendieck's Gauss–Manin ideas.
errors: Minor imprecision: Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology is naturally a K-vector space, K = Frac W(k). The expected finiteness is over K. Over W, the integral dagger de Rham cohomology can have infinitely generated torsion (non-finite-type phenomena). So 'modules de t.f. sur W' is too strong as a literal expectation for the integral theory, although the previous page stresses the W-integral version.

The diagnosis was historically right. Finiteness of MW / rigid cohomology for smooth varieties was proved only in 1997 (Berthelot; also Mebkhout), using de Jong's alterations or p-adic differential equation techniques rather than a Leray dévissage. Relative (Leray-type) theory in rigid cohomology long remained difficult.

ideas.what: Critique of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology: tied to lifting differentials, so limited to smooth X_0; no relative theory or Leray spectral sequence for f: X_0→Y_0, hence no dévissage; hence no proof of finiteness, duality or Künneth
ideas.modern_name: Limitations of Monsky–Washnitzer (dagger) cohomology; finiteness of rigid cohomology; relative rigid cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Critique: Grothendieck (motivation for crystalline cohomology, 1966–68). Finiteness: Berthelot 1997, Mebkhout 1997, later Kedlaya
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES notes, 1966; in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968), which discusses Monsky–Washnitzer and the motivation for crystals

ideas.what: Leray-type spectral sequences / relative cohomology as the essential tool for dévissage in p-adic cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Relative crystalline/rigid cohomology, Gauss–Manin connection, Leray spectral sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Berthelot (crystalline); Chiarellotto–Tsuzuki, Lazda and others (rigid)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (Dix exposés); Berthelot's thesis developed it

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Grothendieck's well-known critique of Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology, which motivated crystalline cohomology and is essentially in his published 1966/68 IHES text. The diagnosis (no relative theory, hence no finiteness) proved prescient, but it is standard folklore.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: 'des [-graves-] critiques : formelles' should read 'des [-graves-] critiques à formuler,'.
'de n'être[?] joint[?] par les différentielles' is more likely 'de n'être donnée/définie que par les différentielles' (reading uncertain).
'il ne semble guère pas[?]' is probably 'il ne semble guère possible (à cette méthode) [de décrire]'.
'des sortes[?] possibles des [-De Rham-] types[?] levés[?]' should read 'des suites spectrales du [-De Rham-] type Leray'.
'— si précisément pour faire un dévissage dans une démonstration' should read '— si précieuses pour faire des dévissages dans les démonstrations'.
'les plus évidentes qui ont un sens[?] dans un théorème[?]' is probably 'les plus évidentes qu'on est en droit d'attendre'.
'Ω^•_{X_k}' may be Ω^•_{X^†} or similar (the lifted dagger algebra); subscript unclear.
